eyebrow: A portal on the art and science of the senses — with a focus on pain
title: Modulation
intro: In neuroscience, the word for treating pain is *modulating* it. In painting and in music, modulation is the blending of rough edges, the synthesis of tone into harmony. One word, three fields — and the spine of this portal.
dial_hint: Drag — art and science are one object at two settings · arrows for another pair test123

pairs.felt_caption: A painting tries to catch what pain *is like* from the inside.
pairs.measured_caption: The same territory, measured: fluorescence-labelled neurons in a mouse spinal cord section — a micrograph from the lab.
pairs.credit: Left — painting, Asmita Sarkar · Right — fluorescence micrograph, Barik Lab, IISc

pairs.felt_caption: Here the artist reworks a real circuit into something closer to feeling — bloom, spark, a private landscape.
pairs.measured_caption: The same circuit, measured: Grpr+ neurons in the parabrachial nucleus, unedited.
pairs.credit: Left — digital work, Asmita Sarkar · Right — fluorescence micrograph, Barik Lab, IISc

pairs.felt_alt: Painting: a tangle of fine filaments in purple and blue, with an eye at the right
pairs.measured_alt: Fluorescence micrograph: D1R neurons in the anterior cingulate cortex, with branching dendrites
pairs.felt_caption: Pain can feel like something that has been rewired — fine filaments pulled tight and tangled.
pairs.measured_caption: Measured: D1R-expressing neurons in the anterior cingulate cortex, with their long, branching dendrites.
pairs.credit: Left — artwork, Asmita Sarkar · Right — fluorescence micrograph, Barik Lab, IISc

pairs.measured_alt: Fluorescence micrograph: IBA1-labelled microglia in the hippocampus
pairs.felt_caption: A touch that has been rewired into pain.
pairs.credit: Left — artwork, Asmita Sarkar · Right — fluorescence micrograph, Barik Lab, IISc

pairs.measured_alt: Fluorescence micrograph: c-Fos activity in the lateral parabrachial nucleus
pairs.felt_caption: Chronic pain, felt as bruise-like spots that do not fade.
pairs.measured_caption: Measured: c-Fos activity (green) in the lateral parabrachial nucleus, a region that lights up in chronic pain.
pairs.credit: Left — artwork, Asmita Sarkar · Right — fluorescence micrograph, Barik Lab, IISc

pairs.felt_alt: Artwork: Sweet Sorrow — a wire and a poppy
pairs.measured_alt: Fluorescence micrograph: tdTomato-labelled fibres from the medial habenula
pairs.felt_caption: Relief that carries its own sorrow: a wire, a poppy.
pairs.measured_caption: Measured: tdTomato-labelled fibres from the medial habenula, a region rich in opioid receptors.
pairs.credit: Left — artwork, Asmita Sarkar · Right — fluorescence micrograph, Barik Lab, IISc

pairs.felt_alt: Artwork: In Blue — a face with closed eyes in teal, purple and ochre washes
pairs.measured_alt: Fluorescence micrograph: c-Fos in the central thalamus
pairs.felt_caption: The sinking feeling that comes with pain-related anxiety.
pairs.measured_caption: Measured: c-Fos activity (green) in the central thalamus.
pairs.credit: Left — artwork, Asmita Sarkar · Right — fluorescence micrograph, Barik Lab, IISc

pairs.measured_caption: Measured: neurons in a mouse thalamus imaged live as cold becomes painful. Each bright patch is one cell's calcium signal.

pairs.felt_alt: Painting: a foot over orange flames and purple washes
pairs.credit: Left — artwork, Asmita Sarkar · Right — still from a miniscope recording, Barik Lab, IISc

pairs.felt_caption: Pushing through pain when other needs and stresses are pulling at you too.
pairs.measured_caption: Measured: the lateral hypothalamus, where needs and stress compete with pain.
pairs.credit: Left — artwork, Asmita Sarkar · Right — fluorescence micrograph, Barik Lab, IISc

quote: The paintings try to catch the experience of pain rather than accurately illustrating any scientific process.
quote_source: Exhibition note — Asmita Sarkar & Arnab Barik
